patients.summary: Administrative assistant who joined the practice healthy at 25, had a 10-week pregnancy loss in 2021, then developed systemic lupus in 2022 with photosensitive rash, cytopenias and two lupus nephritis flares, autoimmune pericarditis, two episodes of lupus-related hemolysis with severe thrombocytopenia (ADAMTS13 normal), and two dehydration illnesses, one with NSAID-associated acute kidney injury. Antiphospholipid testing has been negative. Stable on hydroxychloroquine and low-dose prednisone in 2026.

documents.title: New Patient Visit — Establish Care
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
25 y/o woman establishing care. Moved her primary care here after her old office's hours stopped working with her job; she is an administrative assistant at a property management company and wanted a place she can text.

No complaints today. Feels well. Periods regular. No meds, no supplements.

PMH: none.
PSH: wisdom teeth out as a teenager.
Meds: none.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother has lupus (on treatment, followed by rheumatology). Maternal aunt with rheumatoid arthritis. Paternal grandmother with Hashimoto thyroiditis. No early heart disease or cancers she knows of.
SH: never smoker. Drinks rarely, less than one drink a week. No drugs. Lives in Hadley. Exercises some, walks on weekends.

ROS negative except as above. No joint pain, rashes, mouth sores, or hair loss.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing. HEENT normal, oropharynx clear, no oral lesions. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Joints without swelling or tenderness. Skin clear, no rash. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P
1. Health maintenance. Tdap today (no record of one in the last 10 years). Baseline CBC, CMP, lipids. HIV and hep C screening once, she agrees. Requesting old records for Pap and immunization history; she thinks her last Pap was a couple of years ago and normal, and believes she had the HPV shots in high school.
2. Family history of autoimmune disease. Discussed what symptoms to report (joint swelling, rash, mouth sores, unexplained fatigue). No testing indicated today.

PHQ-2 negative. Return for annual visit next year or sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Fatou, your blood work from Tuesday is all normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, sugar and cholesterol. The HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to do. Good to meet you.

events.reason: Question about working in office during pandemic

documents.title: Question about going in to work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, my office wants some of us back at the front desk two days a week. I'm healthy but I live with my mom who has lupus and takes medicine for it. Is there anything I should do or is that a reason to stay remote? Thank you.

documents.title: RE: Question about going in to work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question. You yourself don't have a condition that puts you at higher risk. Because your mom is on immune-suppressing medicine, it's reasonable to ask your employer for remote work if they can do it, and I'm glad to write a letter supporting that if it would help. If you do go in: mask, distance at the desk, hand hygiene, and change clothes when you get home. Let me know about the letter.

documents.title: RE: Question about going in to work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: That would help, thank you. My manager's name doesn't need to be on it, just to whom it may concern.

documents.title: Work accommodation letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
To whom it may concern,

Fatou Bryant is a patient in our practice. She lives with a household member who takes immunosuppressive medication. I support remote work for her where her duties allow, to reduce exposure risk to that household member during the current pandemic.

Please contact our office with any questions.

Primary Care Physician

Annual. Doing well. Has been working from home most of the spring and summer, back in the office two days a week now. Sleeping OK. Walking most evenings. No complaints.

SH unchanged, never smoker, rare alcohol.

A/P: Healthy 27 y/o.

- Flu shot today.

documents.title: Call re: positive home pregnancy test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt back. Positive home test this AM, LMP about 01/08/21, so roughly 5-6 weeks. Feels fine, mild nausea, no bleeding or pain. Not taking any meds. Excited, a little nervous.

Reviewed: avoid alcohol, no smoking (never smoker), check with us or OB before any new OTC medicine. Gave return precautions for heavy bleeding, one-sided pain, or fainting.

Referral placed to an outside OB group in Northampton for first prenatal visit; front desk to send referral and she will call them today. She will let us know the date.

documents.title: Obstetrics and Gynecology — Procedure Note and Visit Summary
documents.author: obstetrics and gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN GROUP
Date of service: 04/12/2021
Patient: Fatou Bryant  DOB 09/06/1993

Visit summary: G1 at 10 weeks by dates and first-trimester ultrasound at 7 weeks with cardiac activity noted. Presented with cramping and spotting. Transvaginal ultrasound today shows an intrauterine gestation without cardiac activity, consistent with fetal demise. Options reviewed; patient chose uterine evacuation.

Procedure: suction dilation and curettage under MAC. Findings: products of conception obtained, sent to pathology. EBL 50 mL. No complications.

Pathology: chorionic villi and decidua, consistent with products of conception.

Assessment and plan: missed abortion at 10 weeks, uterus evacuated. Reviewed that most first-trimester losses are single events. Because the loss occurred at 10 weeks and her mother has lupus, antiphospholipid antibody testing is reasonable before a future pregnancy; patient may discuss with her PCP or with us at follow-up. Pelvic rest 2 weeks. Bleeding and fever precautions. Postoperative visit 2 weeks.

Allergies: NKDA. Medications: none.

documents.title: PCP call after D&C
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Saw OB records come through, called to check in. Pt had D&C last Monday. Light bleeding only, no fever, cramping minimal. Sad, taking the week off. Has her mom and a friend nearby. Mood: grieving, not hopeless, sleeping OK.

OB mentioned antiphospholipid testing before any future pregnancy. She doesn't have plans to try again right now. Told her we can do that whenever she wants. Offered a visit or a counseling referral if things get heavier; she'll reach out.

documents.title: Office Visit — Fatigue, Joint Pain, Rash
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 28F, mother with SLE. Since about the start of the year she has been worn out, needing to lie down after work, and her wrists and knees ache, worse in the mornings. A pink rash comes up across her cheeks and nose when she is outside; it got bad after a sunny weekend in February. A few mouth sores over the past couple of months that heal on their own. More hair in the shower drain than usual. No fevers, no chest pain, no shortness of breath, no leg swelling, no change in urine. No new meds or supplements. Not pregnant, LMP 2 weeks ago.

O: Vitals as charted. Faint erythema over both malar areas, crossing the nasal bridge. No ulcers visible today. Scalp without patches. Wrists mildly puffy and tender bilaterally, knees with mild tenderness and soft swelling, no effusion to ballot. Hands otherwise normal. Heart regular, no rub or murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P: Photosensitive facial rash, inflammatory arthralgia, oral ulcers, hair thinning, fatigue, strong family history. Concerning for lupus.
- CBC, CMP, UA, ANA, TSH today.
- Rheumatology referral, asked for an early slot.
- Sun protection, SPF 50 daily, hat.
- Acetaminophen for the joints is fine for now; would rather she not lean on ibuprofen until we see her kidney numbers.
Will message results.

documents.title: Results: CBC, CMP, UA, ANA, TSH
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb and platelets mildly low and WBC at the bottom of normal, all new compared with 2019. Cr normal, UA without protein or blood. TSH normal. ANA positive; titer and pattern to follow with the rheumatology workup. Fits the clinical picture. Rheum referral already placed; front desk to call their office today to see if the date can move up.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Fatou. Your ANA test is positive and your red cell and platelet counts are a little low, and your white count is at the low end of normal. Kidney function and urine are normal and so is your thyroid. Taken together with your rash and joint symptoms, this needs a rheumatologist to sort out, and I've asked them to see you soon. Our front desk is calling them to try to move your appointment earlier. Keep up the sunscreen. Call me if you get fevers, chest pain, swelling, or anything that worries you before then.

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you. My mom has been through this so I kind of figured. They gave me April 18. Is that ok or should I push for earlier?

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: April 18 is reasonable since your kidneys are fine. If anything changes before then, message me.

documents.title: Rheumatology Consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE RHEUMATOLOGY GROUP
Date of visit: 04/18/2022
Re: Fatou Bryant, DOB 09/06/1993

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for sending Ms. Bryant, a 28-year-old administrative assistant, for evaluation of a positive ANA.

History: For roughly three months she has had fatigue and pain in the wrists and knees. A facial rash flares whenever she is in the sun. She gets mouth ulcers now and then and has noticed her hair thinning. In April of last year she lost a pregnancy at 10 weeks and had a D&C. Her mother has SLE; a maternal aunt has RA and her paternal grandmother Hashimoto disease. Wisdom teeth removed as a teen. Never smoked; drinks less than once a week. No medications. NKDA.

Examination: Malar rash present. Mild synovitis of both wrists and both knees. Remainder of the examination, including cardiopulmonary, oral, scalp and skin elsewhere, is unremarkable.

Data today: hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL, leukocytes 3,800/uL, platelets 120,000/uL, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, urinalysis normal. ANA positive at 1:640.

Impression:
1. Systemic lupus erythematosus: photosensitive malar rash, oral ulcers, inflammatory arthritis, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia and anemia with a high-titer ANA. No renal involvement on today's urinalysis.
2. Photosensitivity.
3. Mild anemia, part of the above.
4. Prior 10-week pregnancy loss with a family history of lupus: antiphospholipid syndrome is a reasonable concern. Antiphospholipid panel sent today.

Plan:
- Hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice daily. Baseline retinal examination within the first year; we would appreciate your office arranging this locally.
- Prednisone 5 mg daily for the arthritis while hydroxychloroquine takes effect.
- Vitamin D3 2000 units daily and calcium carbonate 600 mg twice daily while on prednisone.
- Strict photoprotection.
- Contraception counseling: she is not planning pregnancy now; we asked her to tell us before trying.
- Return in 3 months with CBC, chemistries and urinalysis.

ADDENDUM 04/20/2022: Lupus anticoagulant not detected. Anticardiolipin IgG and IgM and anti-beta-2 glycoprotein I IgG and IgM all negative. Laboratory criteria for antiphospholipid syndrome are not met; no anticoagulant or aspirin indicated. We will keep the suspected history on her list and revisit testing before any future pregnancy.

Sincerely,
Rheumatology

documents.title: Ophthalmology — Baseline Hydroxychloroquine Screening
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Outside ophthalmology practice. Exam 05/19/2022.
Indication: baseline exam, hydroxychloroquine started 04/2022.
VA 20/20 OD, 20/20 OS. Pupils normal, no APD. IOP 15/16. Anterior segment quiet. Dilated fundus: healthy discs, maculae flat with normal foveal reflex, vessels and periphery normal.
SD-OCT macula: normal foveal contour, ellipsoid zone intact both eyes.
Humphrey 10-2: reliable, full both eyes.
Impression: normal baseline. No retinal toxicity. Annual screening to begin after 5 years of use, sooner if kidney function declines or dose changes.

documents.title: Rheumatology Follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE RHEUMATOLOGY GROUP
Follow-up 07/25/2022

Ms. Bryant returns three months into hydroxychloroquine. Wrist and knee pain much better, morning stiffness 10 minutes. Rash quiet with sunscreen, though she had a mild flare after a beach day in July. No oral ulcers lately. Energy improved but not normal. Taking prednisone 5 mg most days.

Exam: faint residual malar erythema. No synovitis today. No edema.

Labs: counts improving (see attached); creatinine normal; urinalysis without protein.

Plan: continue hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice daily and prednisone 5 mg daily, vitamin D and calcium. Baseline eye exam done in May, normal. Labs every 3 months through your office or ours. Return 4 months.

documents.title: Office Visit — Leg Swelling
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
29F with SLE (dx 4/2022, rheum) on HCQ 200 BID and pred 5. Two weeks of ankle and shin swelling that is worse by evening; her socks leave deep marks. Urine looks foamy in the toilet. Over the summer and into fall the rash and joint aches crept back, and she is tired again. Some mouth sores. No fever, no weight loss, no chest pain or orthopnea, no dyspnea. No NSAIDs. Taking her meds.

Exam: BP 145/90 (repeat similar), first time elevated here. Weight up about 2 kg. Malar erythema. Mild tenderness of MCPs bilaterally. Lungs clear, no JVD. Heart regular, no rub. 2+ pitting edema to mid-shin bilaterally.

A/P: SLE with new edema, foamy urine, hypertension - concern for lupus nephritis.
- UA, BMP, CBC now. Will call with results today.
- Urgent nephrology referral sent; called their intake line myself.
- No NSAIDs. Low salt in the meantime.
- Rheumatology letter cc'd.
ER precautions: shortness of breath, much less urine, chest pain.

documents.title: Results: UA, BMP, CBC
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Cr 2.1 (was 0.9 in April). UA 3+ protein, 3+ blood, RBCs 21-50. Hgb lower than spring, platelets still low. Nephritis picture. Nephrology can see her Monday 10/24; they asked that she bring a 24-hour urine container back, which they will mail. Rheum aware by fax.

documents.title: Call to patient
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Told her the kidney numbers are down and the urine shows inflammation, likely lupus affecting the kidneys. Nephrology Monday 10/24 at 1 pm. She will do the 24-hour collection over the weekend. Reviewed: no ibuprofen or naproxen, low salt, call or go to ED if short of breath or urine drops off. She sounded scared; her mom went through this too. Will check in after the visit.

documents.title: Nephrology Consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEPHROLOGY ASSOCIATES
Seen 10/24/2022
Patient: Fatou Bryant, 29F

Reason for consultation: proteinuria, hematuria and elevated creatinine in SLE.

HPI: Lupus was diagnosed in April of this year by rheumatology and she has been on hydroxychloroquine and low-dose prednisone. Over the last three months fatigue has worsened and the sun-sensitive facial rash and symmetric wrist and knee pain have returned. For two weeks she has had swelling of both lower legs and foamy urine. Occasional mouth ulcers. No fever and no weight loss.

Meds: hydroxychloroquine 200 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily, vitamin D3 2000 units, calcium carbonate 600 mg BID. NKDA.

Exam: BP 145/90. No signs of heart failure; lungs clear without pulmonary edema. Malar rash that spares the nasolabial folds. Mild synovitis of the small joints of the hands. Pitting edema 2+ in both legs.

Data: hemoglobin 10.5 g/dL. Creatinine 2.1 mg/dL against a baseline of 0.9. Urinalysis 3+ protein with numerous red cell casts. 24-hour urine protein 3.5 g. C3 and C4 reduced. Anti-dsDNA elevated. ANA positive.

Assessment: Active lupus nephritis, presenting as a flare with nephrotic-range proteinuria, active sediment and a creatinine more than double baseline, in a patient with systemic activity.

Plan:
1. Prednisone increased to 40 mg daily for two weeks, then down by 5 mg weekly to 5 mg.
2. Continue hydroxychloroquine.
3. Sodium restriction, no NSAIDs.
4. Labs (CMP, CBC, UA) in 3-4 weeks via PCP; we will see her in 3 months.

Thank you for this referral.
Nephrology

Follow-up 01/23/2023

REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 06/20/2023
Patient: Fatou Bryant, 29F

Chief complaint: leg swelling.

HPI: Woman with SLE and a lupus nephritis flare last fall comes in after three weeks of tiredness, achy joints and swollen legs. Says she has put on about 5 kg without trying. Admits she has not been taking her prednisone every day. Takes hydroxychloroquine.

PMH: SLE, lupus nephritis, photosensitivity, history of suspected antiphospholipid syndrome. PSH: D&C, wisdom teeth.
Meds: prednisone 5 mg daily (inconsistent), vitamin D3, calcium carbonate.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: never smoker, rare alcohol, administrative assistant.
Family: mother SLE, maternal aunt RA, paternal grandmother Hashimoto.

Exam: BP 145/90. Pitting edema to the mid-shins bilaterally. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

Results: UA 3+ protein, RBC casts. Creatinine 1.8 (baseline 0.9). Albumin 2.9. Anti-dsDNA elevated. C3 and C4 low. ESR elevated.

MDM: Recurrent lupus nephritis flare. No hyperkalemia, no pulmonary edema, oxygenating normally. Discussed with on-call nephrology, who recommended prednisone 40 mg daily with taper and clinic follow-up rather than admission.

Disposition: discharged. Prednisone 40 mg daily x 14 days then taper by 5 mg per week. Nephrology clinic this week. PCP within one week. Return for shortness of breath, decreased urine, chest pain.

documents.title: ED Follow-up — Nephritis Flare
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen in ED 6/20 for second lupus nephritis flare (Cr 1.8, alb 2.9, 3+ protein with casts). Sent home on pred 40 with taper. Day 6 of 40 mg. Swelling a bit better since Saturday. Not sleeping well.

We talked about the prednisone. She had been skipping it a few days a week since spring, mostly because she felt fine and hated the hunger and puffiness. HCQ she takes most days. Reviewed why the low dose matters for her kidneys. She wants to be on as little prednisone as possible, which is fair; asked her to raise that with rheum and nephrology instead of stopping on her own.

Exam: BP 142/88. Weight up about 5 kg from her usual. Pitting edema to mid-shin. Lungs clear. Malar area clear.

A/P
Lupus nephritis flare: on prednisone 40 then taper per nephrology. BMP and UA today. Nephrology visit was moved to 8/14 (their first opening); asked them to call if Cr rising.
BP elevated with flare, as before; recheck after taper.
Low salt. No NSAIDs.
RTC after nephrology.

documents.title: Monday's labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Creatinine a touch better than in the ED and potassium is fine. Still a lot of protein in the urine, which is expected this early. Stay on the 40 mg and the taper exactly as written, and call me if the swelling gets worse or you notice less urine.

Follow-up 08/14/2023

Seen after the June flare. Prednisone taper finished; on 5 mg daily, which she says she is now taking every day. Edema gone. Weight back to her usual.

BP 122/78. No edema.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 06/23/2024  Discharged 06/28/2024
Patient: Fatou Bryant, 30F
Attending service: hospital medicine; consultants hematology, rheumatology, nephrology.

Reason for admission: microangiopathic hemolytic anemia with platelets 20,000, creatinine 2.5 and confusion in a patient with SLE and lupus nephritis.

Hospital course:
TTP was the immediate concern. Daily therapeutic plasma exchange began the night of admission, along with IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for three doses. ADAMTS13 activity returned on 06/25 at 52%, which argues against TTP, and plasma exchange was stopped after the third session. Hemolysis and thrombocytopenia were attributed to active lupus. Antiphospholipid testing was repeated: lupus anticoagulant not detected, anticardiolipin and anti-beta-2 glycoprotein I antibodies negative. Headache and confusion cleared by hospital day 2 and the remaining neurologic exam was normal. Jaundice faded. Platelets and hemoglobin rose steadily after steroids; no transfusion needed. Creatinine improved with treatment of the flare. Blood pressure normalized as she improved.

Discharge data: platelets 138,000, hemoglobin 8.4, creatinine 1.4.

Discharge diagnoses: SLE flare with microangiopathic hemolysis and thrombocytopenia; lupus nephritis.

Discharge medications:
- Prednisone 60 mg daily; rheumatology to direct the taper.
- Hydroxychloroquine 200 mg BID (continue).
- Vitamin D3 2000 units daily, calcium carbonate 600 mg BID (continue).
Stopped: prednisone 5 mg (replaced by above).

Follow-up: PCP within one week (CBC, BMP, hepatic panel). Hematology in 6 weeks. Rheumatology in 2 weeks.
Allergies: NKDA.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL — NEPHROLOGY SERVICE DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 04/27/2025 via the emergency department. Discharged 04/30/2025.
Patient: Fatou Bryant, 31F. NKDA.

Presentation: Three days of severe vomiting and diarrhea, unable to keep fluids down, much like the illness that brought her to the ED last October. For abdominal cramping she had been taking ibuprofen every 4 hours.
On arrival BP 90/60, HR 110. Lethargic, mucous membranes dry, poor skin turgor.

Data: creatinine 2.1 (baseline 0.9), BUN 40, potassium 3.5, bicarbonate 24. Urine sodium 10, urine osmolality 500.

Assessment: acute kidney injury, prerenal from volume depletion, with NSAID use contributing; dehydration from gastrointestinal losses.

Course: IV isotonic fluids, antiemetics, ibuprofen stopped. Hydroxychloroquine and prednisone continued. Diarrhea settled by day 2, tolerating diet day 3. Creatinine 1.1 on the morning of discharge.

Discharge medications: hydroxychloroquine 200 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily, vitamin D3, calcium carbonate. STOP ibuprofen and all NSAIDs; acetaminophen for pain.

TCM. Admitted 10/23-10/29 for recurrent lupus-related microangiopathic hemolysis with plt 20k, Hgb 7.8, bili 2.2; ADAMTS13 58%, plasma exchange x2, pulse methylpred, now prednisone 60 with taper per rheum. Discharge summary reviewed; med rec done.

Feels weak but improving daily. No nosebleeds since the hospital. Urine clear. No fever. Appetite big, sleep broken on the steroid. Out of work until 11/17.

Meds: prednisone 60 mg daily (taper), HCQ 200 BID, D3, calcium. No NSAIDs.

Exam: vitals as charted. No icterus. No petechiae. Nares clear. Heart regular, lungs clear. No edema. Neuro normal.

A/P
1. Recurrent SLE hemolysis with thrombocytopenia: CBC, CMP today; next CBC with hematology in January unless symptoms. She asked about prevention of another episode - forwarded her question to rheum and hematology with today's labs.
2. Steroid effects: glucose today; sleep hygiene.
3. Flu shot today (counts adequate, no contraindication).
4. Work note; FMLA forms to complete.
RTC 6-8 weeks.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:

Fatou Bryant was hospitalized 10/23/2025 to 10/29/2025 and remains under my care. She may return to work on 11/17/2025.

Primary Care Physician

documents.title: Tuesday's labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Platelets are back in the normal range and hemoglobin is rising. Bilirubin is normal again, kidneys fine, sugar OK on the prednisone. Sent to hematology and rheumatology.

documents.title: FMLA forms
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: FMLA certification from employer completed by PCP and faxed to HR. Covers 10/23/2025 through 11/16/2025 continuous, plus intermittent leave for flares and appointments for one year. Copy to pt via portal.

documents.title: Rheumatology Visit — Taper Plan
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE RHEUMATOLOGY GROUP
Visit 11/17/2025

Seen after the October admission, the second episode of SLE-associated microangiopathic hemolysis with thrombocytopenia; ADAMTS13 58%, antiphospholipid antibodies negative. Back at work today. No bleeding or dark urine. PCP labs from 11/4 reviewed: platelets normal, hemoglobin rising, bilirubin normal.

Exam: no petechiae, no synovitis, no rash.

Plan: prednisone taper from 60 mg, down 10 mg weekly to 20 mg, then 15 mg and 10 mg for two weeks each, then 5 mg daily by mid-January. Continue hydroxychloroquine 200 mg BID. Her question about preventing another episode noted from the PCP; we will go through it at the January visit with hematology's input. Return January.

documents.title: Hematology Follow-up
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HEMATOLOGY-ONCOLOGY GROUP
Visit 01/20/2026

Seen 12 weeks after the October admission for the second episode of SLE-associated microangiopathic hemolysis with thrombocytopenia. ADAMTS13 normal on both occasions (52% in 2024, 58% in 2025); antiphospholipid testing repeatedly negative. TTP and APS are not the explanation.

Feels well. No bleeding, dark urine or neurologic symptoms. Prednisone taper finished this week.

Labs: hemoglobin 11.4, platelets 205,000, LDH and haptoglobin normal.

Impression: in remission. Further prevention rests on lupus control, which rheumatology is directing.
Plan: CBC every 3 months via PCP, and urgently with dark urine, bleeding, headache or confusion. Return 6 months.

documents.title: Rheumatology Follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE RHEUMATOLOGY GROUP
Visit 01/20/2026

Ms. Bryant returns after the October hemolysis admission. Taper complete; back on prednisone 5 mg daily as of this week. Taking hydroxychloroquine faithfully. No joint pain, rash, oral ulcers, chest pain or swelling. Hematology saw her this morning: counts normal.

Exam: well. No synovitis, no rash, no rub, no edema.

Assessment: SLE, currently quiet after a second hematologic flare; thrombocytopenia resolved. Kidney function and proteinuria stable per her PCP's labs.

Plan: continue hydroxychloroquine 200 mg BID and prednisone 5 mg daily, vitamin D and calcium. She asked how to prevent another episode; we went over daily hydroxychloroquine, steady prednisone and early calls for dark urine or bleeding. Labs every 3 months through PCP. Return 4 months.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit — SLE Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after hematology and rheum in January (letters reviewed: counts normal, taper done, prednisone 5 again, staying on current regimen). Back at work since November. Energy good. No bleeding, dark urine, headache, rash, joint pain or swelling.

Meds: HCQ 200 BID, prednisone 5 daily, D3, calcium. No NSAIDs.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. No pallor or petechiae. Heart regular, lungs clear. No synovitis. No edema.

A/P
1. SLE, quiet. CBC every 3 months per heme.
2. Lupus nephritis: BMP, UA, UPCR today.
3. Anemia, at her usual.
RTC 3 months.
